prompt:
Scene:
A square photograph at deep winter twilight in subarctic tundra, 35mm medium-format camera at ground level. Snow-covered flats stretching to a distant mountain silhouette; violet sky overhead.

Subject:
A frozen tundra pond has erupted with a vertical geyser of liquid water that refuses to return. The column ascends 80 meters and continues rising at visible speed, its surface partially freezing into glittering ice crystals that float upward with the flow. At the top, a cloud of slowly rising ice flakes disperses into the cold sky like a negative snowfall.

Important details:
Hyper-cold aesthetics: every surface ice-rimed, fine hoarfrost on tundra vegetation. Steam billows immediately where hot geyser water meets minus-twenty air. A scientist in a red arctic parka stands at 30 meters' distance as scale anchor. Moon visible at upper-right. Footprints in snow lead toward the geyser and stop.

Use case:
Lift-studies single 4/5 — reverse gravity in frozen biome with partial-freeze physics.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no aurora (reserve for other topic), no brand gear, no polar bears, no stylized illustration.
